subject: Thales2b elevated 5xx trend — customer notice & follow-up actions
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: [INTERNAL] Thales2b — rising 5xx and timeout pattern (first detection)

Team,

We started seeing a sustained increase in 5xx responses for the Thales2b family at ~08:00 UTC this morning. Key observations: 
- Scope: ~3–4% of requests across thales2b-small and thales2b-medium variants (not the larger rollout).
- Error types: a mix of 502/503 and request timeouts (client-side 504).
- Onset: sudden from a ~0.3% baseline to the current rate over ~15 minutes.
- Impact window: 08:00–08:30 UTC spike; sporadic tailing errors after 08:30.

I've attached a small extract of metrics (thales2b-metrics-0502.csv) showing request rate, error-rate, and latency percentiles per instance. Initial triage points: 
1) Autoscaler saw a surge and started provisioning; several pods reported KV cache misses and a subsequent backlog in the request queue.
2) We observed a handful of gRPC stream resets on the V2 inference path coincident with instance flapping.
3) No obvious model weight corruption; model loads completed successfully.

Immediate asks: 
- Dev: can you validate whether the KV cache invalidation/fallback path is triggering a synchronous cold load that blocks token generation? Suspect a race in the cache invalidator + batcher handoff.
- Marissa/Ben: prepare an outbound customer notice for any accounts hitting >=2% 5xx in the last 30m. Keep it short — what we saw, what we're doing, ETA for next update.

Proposed mitigation (short-term): throttle new requests to thales2b-medium, promote routing to thales2b-stable variants if available, and increase aggressive autoscaler headroom while we patch.

I'll follow up once we have a concrete root cause.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anton Rivera <anton@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Thales2b — brief customer notice (Bluecrest Analytics)

Anton,

Quick heads-up from Redwood: between ~08:00–08:30 UTC we detected an elevated rate of 5xx and timeout errors affecting the Thales2b model variants used by your account. We have identified the issue as a service-level degradation (autoscaler + cache handoff) and have taken the following immediate actions: 
- Redirected new traffic away from thales2b-medium to more stable model variants where possible.
- Increased autoscaler headroom to reduce provisioning latency for active queues.
- Deployed an emergency hotfix to the batcher handoff (rolling across regions) — initial rollout completed at ~09:30 UTC.

What you may have seen: failed generation calls (502/503) and occasional long waits followed by timeouts. If you have request IDs or logs for failed queries, please send them across and we'll correlate.

ETA/commitment: We expect error rates to be back to baseline within 60–90 minutes after the fix was deployed; we will confirm once the final validation completes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts runtime SLAs. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and action items tomorrow.

Best,
Dylan

Attachments: thales2b-metrics-0502.csv
--
Dylan Brooks
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Anton Rivera <anton@bluecrest.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@bluecrest.ai
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 09:02:14 +0000
Subject: Re: Thales2b — brief customer notice (Bluecrest Analytics)

Thanks for the quick update, Dylan.

We saw a spike in 502s across our nightly batch run that started at ~08:10 UTC; it matches what you describe. We've pulled logs for the failing calls and attached them (bluecrest-request-logs.txt). A couple of request IDs included in the attach: bca-20290502-17, bca-20290502-42.

Please let us know if you need anything else from our side. The customer-facing pipelines rely on Thales2b for summarization; this caused retries and delayed downstream processing.

Anton
Head of Platform Engineering
Bluecrest Analytics

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2029 14:20:00 +0000
Subject: Thales2b incident — RCA and action items (postmortem summary)

Follow-up summary (root cause + remediation):

Root cause: a race condition in the KV cache invalidation path combined with aggressive autoscaler termination created a window where batcher workers attempted to serve from an invalidated cache. That triggered synchronous cold-model fallback loads while the batcher held token-generation locks, resulting in request queue growth and gRPC stream resets. The combination manifested as elevated 502/503 errors and client timeouts for certain thales2b variants.

Timeline (UTC):
- 08:00 — error rate begins rising; internal alert triggers.
- 08:10 — customers (example: Bluecrest) report failures.
- 08:18 — triage identifies correlation with recent cache invalidation change (deployed 2029-04-29).
- 08:30 — temporary routing rules applied to shift traffic off thales2b-medium.
- 09:10 — emergency patch to batcher handoff pushed to canary.
- 09:30 — patch rolled to all active regions; error rates return to baseline by ~10:05.

Remediation deployed: immediate hotfix to synchronize cache invalidation and batcher handoff; conservative autoscaler termination policy applied (longer drain window).

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Dev: add unit/integration test for cache invalidation handoff (Dev Patel) — ETA 2029-05-17.
- Infra: adjust autoscaler drain timeout for all model runtimes (Ben Carter) — ETA 2029-05-10.
- Product/CS: send a short customer-facing postmortem and credits proposal for impacted SLAs (Marissa Cole) — draft by 2029-05-04.
- Eng+SRE: add a focused alert that specifically tracks gRPC stream resets correlated with cache invalidations (Dev + SRE) — ETA 2029-05-09.

Attachments: postmortem-thales2b-0503.pdf (detailed charts, traces, and remediation checklist).

Thanks to everyone who triaged overnight. We'll follow up with the customer communication once Marissa has the note ready.

Dev
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
